unit.scope_boundary: Only the scalar 32-bit bit-size form and.b32 d, a, b; is in scope. The .pred, .b16, and .b64 forms of the same section and the sibling logic/shift instructions are out of scope (PTX-AND-SEM2-003/064; architecture D-0c/D-24). Source operand a is register-only: every read example uses a register in position a, and whether a may be a constant immediate is an open question (PTX-AND-SEM2-023/025/061), so no immediate constructor is introduced for position a (adding one would assert permissibility not present in the approved interpretation). Source operand b is a register variable or a constant immediate: the official example 'and.b32  sign,fpvalue,0x80000000;' directly evidences an immediate (0x80000000) in source position b for the .b32 form (PTX-AND-SEM2-024), so the Lean mapping carries SourceB.reg and SourceB.imm. The bit bucket '_' is a candidate alternative destination at the strength of the general section 9.2 rule (architecture SF-A13; PTX-AND-SEM2-062). No error/trap/undefined/implementation-defined behavior is invented (PTX-AND-SEM2-048/049/050). Version/target metadata is not modeled as execution behavior (PTX-AND-SEM2-046/047/059; architecture VAL-5/VAL-6).

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that the execution relation AndB32Step is deterministic: for any state s and instruction i, at most one resulting state is related. This is the derived determinism interpretation PTX-AND-SEM2-038 (determinism NOT explicitly stated in the source), realized non-vacuously over the relational semantics per design D-25 / PTX-AND-SEM2-057. Because AndB32Step is a Prop-valued inductive relation and not a function, the theorem is not a definitional triviality: it must rule out the possibility that both the guardFalse and executed constructors (or two executions) relate distinct resulting states.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every machine state s, instruction i, and states s1, s2: if AndB32Step s i s1 and AndB32Step s i s2, then s1 = s2.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem andB32Step_deterministic
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState)
    (h1 : AndB32Step s i s1) (h2 : AndB32Step s i s2) :
    s1 = s2
hypotheses: h1 : AndB32Step s i s1 (the relation admits a step from s on i to s1)
h2 : AndB32Step s i s2 (the relation admits a step from s on i to s2)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: s1 = s2 (at most one resulting state).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Derived interpretation PTX-AND-SEM2-038 (determinism; not explicitly stated in the source); design dependency PTX-AND-SEM2-057 (D-25 relational representation so that determinism is non-vacuous); design dependency PTX-AND-SEM2-058 (two-case outcome executed/guardFalse, no error constructor). Source evidence: AND_SEMANTICS ('d = a & b;'), AND_DESCRIPTION ('Compute the bit-wise and operation for the bits in a and b.'), CTX-02 (guard evaluation), CTX-08 (predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction'). No arithmetic-result assumption is involved because the bitwise-and is a pure bit-wise operation over two fixed 32-bit values.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation is inhabited: the executable example with r1 = 5, r2 = 3 and unguarded and.b32 r1, r1, r2 (aliasing d == a, demonstrated by #eval: r1 becomes 5 & 3 = 1) yields an AndB32Step from the executed constructor; the @p with p = false example (r1 stays 5) yields an AndB32Step from the guardFalse constructor. The conclusion s1 = s2 is not an element of the hypotheses; the theorem excludes a hypothetical relation that admitted two distinct results. This is the meaningful relational determinism property required by D-25; the trivial single-valuedness of the total function execAndB32 is NOT this obligation (see traceability_summary.determinism_note).
strength_risks: The theorem must not be misread as functional totality of execAndB32; it is a relational property over AndB32Step only.

The proof is a short case analysis on the two constructors using disjointness of evalGuard outcomes (some false vs some true) and is appropriate; the reviewer should confirm the statement adds no unapproved totality or totality-on-well-formed-domain precondition.
The theorem does not assert existence of a step (that is a completeness/correspondence matter, PTX-AND-THM-002); it asserts uniqueness when a step exists.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on h1 and h2. If both come from the guardFalse constructor, the conclusion is reflexivity (s1 = s and s2 = s). If both come from the executed constructor, both give the same post-state updateDestination s i.d (andValue va vb) with (possibly) different va/vb values, but each constructor premise fixes evalSourceA s i.a and evalSourceB s i.b to the respective values, so injectivity of some (Option) yields va1 = va2 and vb1 = vb2 (the result value andValue va vb is then equal by congruence). If one is guardFalse and the other executed, the premises force evalGuard s i.guard = some false and evalGuard s i.guard = some true respectively, contradicting the disjointness of the two Option Bool values; derive False.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-1 (determinism of the execution relation).

theorem_obligations.category: function/relation correspondence (PRF-1 family; Lean file deferred item)
theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the correspondence between the executable function execAndB32 and the relational semantics AndB32Step. This is the item explicitly deferred by the Lean mapping itself (AndB32-v1.lean lines 335-347, section 14 comment block: 'The correspondence between the relation and the executable function is a theorem-stage obligation (PRF-1 family)') and consistent with mapping-critic F-5 (theorem obligations deferred to the theorem-design stage). The correspondence has four parts: (a)-(b) soundness (every outcome of the function is a step), (c) completeness (every step is realized by some function outcome), and (d) partial-completeness (function partiality none occurs exactly when the relation admits no step). Part (d) makes the partial-execution convention (Option none = partial execution for out-of-domain states, not an error; PTX-AND-SEM2-048/049/050) precise with respect to the relation.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) If execAndB32 s i returns some (ExecOutcome.executed s'), then AndB32Step s i s'. (b) If execAndB32 s i returns some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s'), then AndB32Step s i s'. (c) If AndB32Step s i s', then there exists an outcome o with execAndB32 s i = some o and o is either ExecOutcome.executed s' or ExecOutcome.guardFalse s'. (d) execAndB32 s i = none if and only if there is no state s' with AndB32Step s i s'.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem exec_sound_executed
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) :
    AndB32Step s i s'

theorem exec_sound_guardFalse
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')) :
    AndB32Step s i s'

theorem step_complete
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : AndB32Step s i s') :
    Exists fun (o : ExecOutcome) =>
      execAndB32 s i = some o /\
      (o = ExecOutcome.executed s' \/ o = ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')

theorem step_partial_complete
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) :
    execAndB32 s i = none <->
      not (Exists fun (s' : MachineState) => AndB32Step s i s')
hypotheses: Parts (a), (b), (d) quantify over arbitrary states and instructions; no additional preconditions are added.
Part (c) takes h : AndB32Step s i s' and concludes the existence of a corresponding function outcome.
theorem_obligations.conclusion: The four stated equivalences/implications between execAndB32 and AndB32Step.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Design dependency PTX-AND-SEM2-057 (D-25 relational representation; relation/function correspondence is a theorem-stage obligation in the PRF-1 family); design dependency PTX-AND-SEM2-058 (two-case outcome, no error constructor); DERIVED bitwise-and semantics PTX-AND-SEM2-032, guard-true behavior PTX-AND-SEM2-033, and guard-false state effect PTX-AND-SEM2-063 (source-resolved via CTX-08 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.'). Partiality convention PTX-AND-SEM2-048/049/050 (no invented error/UB; Option none is partial execution). Source evidence: AND_SEMANTICS, CTX-08.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable witnesses for every part exist among the executable examples: part (b) via the @p with p = false example (guardFalse outcome; also a guardFalse step), part (a) via the aliasing d == a example (executed outcome; also an executed step), part (c) via both of those steps, and part (d) via the partial-execution example (missing source register yields none and no step). The conclusions are not elements of the hypotheses; each direction requires unfolding the definitions of both the function and the relation and is the substantive bridge deferred by the Lean file.
strength_risks: Part (d) must not be misread as asserting totality over all states; none for out-of-domain states is partiality (PTX-AND-SEM2-048/049/050; risk R-2).

The relation omits the none partial case (it relates only complete executions); this is a mapping decision consistent with D-25 (mapping-critic F-5) and the correspondence makes it precise rather than hiding it.
The reviewer should confirm the four statements add no unapproved preconditions and use exactly the constructors of ExecOutcome.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: All four parts unfold execAndB32 and AndB32Step and case-split on evalGuard (Option Bool: none/some false/some true) and, where the executed branch is reached, on evalSourceA for i.a and then on evalSourceB for i.b (Option B32; evalSourceB covers both SourceB.reg and SourceB.imm). Part (a): with h, the evalGuard match took the some true branch and both source matches the some va / some vb branches; instantiate the executed constructor. Part (b): the evalGuard match took the some false branch; instantiate the guardFalse constructor (note ExecOutcome.guardFalse s' forces s' = s). Part (c): case on the step constructor; for guardFalse, hguard : evalGuard = some false gives the guardFalse outcome; for executed, hguard, ha, and hb give the executed outcome with o = ExecOutcome.executed s'. Part (d): forward by cases on evalGuard/evalSourceA/evalSourceB; reverse by showing each constructor would contradict execAndB32 = none.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-1 family (determinism and relation/function correspondence); AndB32-v1.lean lines 335-347.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the bitwise-and fidelity property: when the guard is true, the destination is a register r, and both sources resolve in the pre-instruction state s, the value written to r equals the bitwise-and of the values read from the two sources. This is the Semantics line 'd = a & b;' (AND_SEMANTICS; SOURCE_FACT PTX-AND-SEM2-008) and the derived bitwise-and semantics PTX-AND-SEM2-032 (bitwise-and over the 32-bit untyped .b32 value domain; no arithmetic, truncation, or rounding). The statement uses evalSourceB for the second source, which covers both the register-source case (AND_B32_EXAMPLE_1 'and.b32  x,q,r;') and the immediate-source case (AND_B32_EXAMPLE_2 'and.b32  sign,fpvalue,0x80000000;' with the immediate 0x80000000 in position b; PTX-AND-SEM2-024), uniformly: when i.b = SourceB.imm v, evalSourceB s i.b = some v and the written value is andValue va v. Because the source values are read from the pre-instruction state s (not from any post-update state), the statement also subsumes the read-before-write aliasing behavior PTX-AND-SEM2-060: when i.a or i.b (as a register) aliases the destination r, the values va/vb are the pre-update values of r, and the destination receives the bitwise-and of those pre-update values (demonstrated by the executable examples: d == a with r1 = 5, r2 = 3 gives r1 becomes 5 & 3 = 1; self-aliasing d == a == b with r1 = 5 gives r1 becomes 5 & 5 = 5). The exact formal statement is the semantic-phase matter OQ-8 / PTX-AND-SEM2-068; this is the proposed formalization for theorem-strength review.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, register r, and B32 values va, vb: if the complete guard expression evaluates true in s, i.d is the register destination r, evalSourceA s i.a = some va, and evalSourceB s i.b = some vb (both sources resolve in the pre-instruction state s; vb is either a register value or the immediate value of position b), then execAndB32 s i returns the executed outcome with some post-state s' and s'.valueRegs r = some (andValue va vb). The equality pins the written value to the bitwise-and of the values read from the pre-instruction state, which is exactly the and rule and the read-before-write aliasing behavior.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAndB32_and_fidelity
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true)
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r)
    (ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va)
    (hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb) :
    Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
      execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /\
      s'.valueRegs r = some (andValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true (the complete guard expression is true, including the unguarded case)
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r (the destination is the register r; the bit-bucket destination is handled by PTX-AND-THM-005)
ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va (the first source resolves in the pre-instruction state s; va is the pre-update value)
hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb (the second source resolves in the pre-instruction state s; vb is the pre-update register value or the immediate value)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exists s' : MachineState, execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /\ s'.valueRegs r = some (andValue va vb), i.e. the value written to r equals the bitwise-and of the values read from the two sources (register or immediate for position b).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: SOURCE_FACT PTX-AND-SEM2-008 (Semantics 'd = a & b;', AND_SEMANTICS); DERIVED bitwise-and semantics PTX-AND-SEM2-032 (grounded in AND_SEMANTICS, AND_DESCRIPTION, AND_TARGET_SECTION, CTX-04, CTX-03); DERIVED guard-true behavior PTX-AND-SEM2-033; DERIVED source read PTX-AND-SEM2-034; DERIVED destination write PTX-AND-SEM2-036; DERIVED read-before-write PTX-AND-SEM2-060; OPEN_QUESTION PTX-AND-SEM2-068 (OQ-8: exact Lean statement of the and-fidelity candidate obligation PRF-7). The immediate-source-b coverage relies on the DERIVED claim PTX-AND-SEM2-024 (official example AND_B32_EXAMPLE_2: and.b32 sign,fpvalue,0x80000000;).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable examples 0&0=0, 0xFFFFFFFF&0xFFFFFFFF=0xFFFFFFFF, 5&3=1, 0xFFFF0000&0x00FF00FF=0x00FF0000=16711680, the register-source example (q = 0xFFFF0000, r = 0x00FF00FF gives x = 16711680), the official example shape (0xFFFFFFFF & 0x80000000 = 2147483648), the immediate-source-b example (r1 becomes 5 & 3 = 1 with b = imm 3), the aliasing d == a example (r1 becomes 5 & 3 = 1), and the self-aliasing d == a == b example (r1 becomes 5 & 5 = 5). The conclusion (the written value is exactly andValue va vb) is not an element of the hypotheses; it pins the destination write to the bitwise-and of the pre-state source reads and distinguishes and semantics from copy semantics, any other transformation, truncation, or read-after-write semantics.
strength_risks: The equality s'.valueRegs r = some (andValue va vb) relies on andValue being the bitwise-and over the 32-bit domain (the and rule d = a & b; PTX-AND-SEM2-008/032; Lean representation Nat.land modulo 2^32 per mapping-critic F-4). The statement is written so that any faithful implementation of andValue satisfies it; the reviewer should keep the and-fidelity dependency explicit.
The theorem must keep va and vb defined from the pre-instruction state s (never from the post-state s'), or the read-before-write content (PTX-AND-SEM2-060) would be lost.
The theorem does not assert behavior for missing registers; those are out-of-domain partiality (PTX-AND-SEM2-048/049/050; risk R-2).

The statement covers position-b immediates through evalSourceB; it does not assert that position a may be an immediate (open question PTX-AND-SEM2-061; SourceA has no imm constructor, so the theorem cannot be instantiated with an immediate first source).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAndB32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some true branch; with ha and hb the evalSourceA and evalSourceB matches select some va and some vb; the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed (updateDestination s i.d (andValue va vb))). With hd : i.d = Destination.reg r, unfold updateDestination and simplify the valueRegs update function (fun r' => if r' == r then some (andValue va vb) else s.valueRegs r') with the DecidableEq of RegId to conclude s'.valueRegs r = some (andValue va vb). The aliasing cases i.a = SourceA.reg r and/or i.b = SourceB.reg r follow with ha/hb : evalSourceA s (SourceA.reg r) = some va / evalSourceB s (SourceB.reg r) = some vb and the source evaluators unfolding to s.valueRegs r = some va/vb, i.e. the pre-update values. The immediate case i.b = SourceB.imm v follows with evalSourceB s (SourceB.imm v) = some v by definition.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-7 (and-fidelity: the value written equals the bitwise-and of the values read, 'd = a & b;', AND_SEMANTICS); read-before-write aspect of PTX-AND-SEM2-060.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the destination-only update / frame property over the execution relation: when a step executes with a register destination r, the only value register that may change is r; every other value register and every predicate register is unchanged. This is the relational frame obligation (architecture PRF-2; semantics future topic PRF-2) grounded in DERIVED claims PTX-AND-SEM2-036 (only the destination register is updated) and PTX-AND-SEM2-037 (write locality: no memory, special-register, carry-flag, status-register, or condition-code component is written by the bounded base and.b32). The statement is made over the bounded model (value-register file plus predicate-register file) and retains the documented negative-evidence caveat: the bounded model contains no carry-flag/status components, and the absence of such writes is absence-based negative evidence (PTX-AND-SEM2-037/048/049/050; risk R-1), not an affirmative NVIDIA enumeration; the frame claim must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, related state s', and register r: if AndB32Step s i s' and i.d is the register destination r, then (1) every value register r' different from r has the same value in s' as in s; and (2) every predicate register p has the same value in s' as in s. The theorem holds in both the executed and the guard-false cases (in the guard-false case s' = s, so the frame is trivially satisfied; the executed case is the content).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem andB32Step_destination_only_frame
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (r : RegId)
    (hstep : AndB32Step s i s')
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) :
    (forall (r' : RegId), r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\
    (forall (p : PredId), s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p)
hypotheses: hstep : AndB32Step s i s' (the relation admits a step from s on i to s')
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r (the destination is the register r)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (forall r', r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\ (forall p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED claims PTX-AND-SEM2-036 (state write: destination register d updated with the bitwise-and of the values read from a and b; the source states no other register write) and PTX-AND-SEM2-037 (write locality: only the destination update required by the bounded semantics; no memory/special-register/carry/status component written); PTX-AND-SEM2-054 (minimal state pair). Source evidence: AND_SEMANTICS, AND_DESCRIPTION, AND_SYNTAX_FORM. The absence of carry/status writes is NEGATIVE evidence (PTX-AND-SEM2-037/048/049/050; risk R-1).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example with r1 = 1, r2 = 2 and updateDestination (Destination.reg r1) (mkB32 100) shows r1 becomes 100 while r2 remains 2 and the predicate file is untouched. The conclusion (all other value registers and all predicates preserved) is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the frame content and distinguishes destination-only semantics from any semantics writing additional state.
strength_risks: Risk R-1 (PTX-AND-SEM2-037/048/049/050): the theorem must be stated over the bounded model only and must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement that 'no carry flag / status register is written'. The absence-based caveat must remain traceable until final acceptance.

The theorem does not assert the value written to r itself (that is PTX-AND-THM-003); a reviewer should ensure no attempt to strengthen this theorem into an assertion about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on hstep. The guardFalse constructor gives s' = s, so both conjuncts are by reflexivity. The executed constructor gives s' = updateDestination s i.d (andValue va vb); with hd : i.d = Destination.reg r, unfold updateDestination: the valueRegs function becomes fun r' => if r' == r then some (andValue va vb) else s.valueRegs r'. Use by_cases (r' == r) on the DecidableEq of RegId to prove r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r'; predicate registers are untouched because only the valueRegs field is updated in the record (predRegs equality by record simplification).
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-2 (destination-only update / frame), with negative-evidence caveat from risk R-1.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the bit-bucket discard property over the execution relation: when the destination is the bit bucket '_', a step changes no value register and the whole state is unchanged (s' = s). This corresponds to semantics future topic PRF-3. The obligation retains the documented strength caveat: the no-write consequence is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (architecture SF-A13, recorded in foundation-v1.md; open question PTX-AND-SEM2-062/AMB-3); the scalar and.b32 section does not demonstrate the bit-bucket form, so the theorem must not be presented as an and.b32-specific explicit source fact (mapping-critic F-3).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, and related state s': if AndB32Step s i s' and i.d is the bit bucket Destination.bitBucket, then s' = s: the computed value is discarded and no value register or predicate register changes. The strength of this claim is limited to the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (architecture SF-A13; PTX-AND-SEM2-062).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem andB32Step_bit_bucket_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (hstep : AndB32Step s i s')
    (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket) :
    s' = s
hypotheses: hstep : AndB32Step s i s' (the relation admits a step from s on i to s')
hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket (the destination is the bit bucket '_')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: s' = s (the related state is exactly the input state; the result is discarded).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED claim PTX-AND-SEM2-022 (destination register for the bounded base; whether the bit bucket '_' is permitted is an open question); OPEN_QUESTION PTX-AND-SEM2-062 (OQ-2: whether '_' is permitted for the scalar and.b32 form; the general section 9.2 rule is architecture-recorded SF-A13 but is not in this bundle); design dependency PTX-AND-SEM2-058 (execution outcome representation).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example with the bit bucket destination keeps r1 at 1 (no value register written), demonstrating the no-write behavior; a guard-false step with bit bucket destination also satisfies s' = s. The conclusion s' = s is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the discard content and distinguishes the bit-bucket destination from the register destination (PTX-AND-THM-003/004).
strength_risks: Risk R-3 (AMB-3 / PTX-AND-SEM2-062 / mapping-critic F-3): the theorem must not be presented as and.b32-specific explicit NVIDIA behavior; it is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 rule (architecture SF-A13). PRF-3 strength must not exceed this.

If the theorem-strength review decides the bit-bucket constructor should be deferred until the scalar applicability question (PTX-AND-SEM2-062) is resolved, this obligation is removed or weakened accordingly; the current statement is faithful to the Gate-C-approved Lean mapping, which materializes the constructor at candidate strength (mapping-critic F-3).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on hstep. The guardFalse constructor gives s' = s directly. The executed constructor gives s' = updateDestination s i.d (andValue va vb); with hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket, unfold updateDestination: the bitBucket branch returns s, so s' = s; simp.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-3 (bit-bucket discard), with AMB-3 strength caveat.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the instruction is not executed and the machine state is unchanged. This is the guard-false frame property (semantics future topic PRF-4), grounded in the DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-AND-SEM2-063, which is source-resolved via the official section 9.7.13.2 clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (CTX-08; SOURCE_FACT PTX-AND-SEM2-071; derivation chain PTX-AND-SEM2-074). It is NOT a human assumption and must never be presented as one. The functional form (a) states that the guard-false outcome carries exactly the input state, so no value-register or predicate-register component changes; it also entails that source operands are NOT read in this branch (the code returns before evaluating sources), matching the mapping decision recorded by mapping-critic F-1 and consistent with the approved 'do nothing' reading. The relational form (b) states the same over AndB32Step.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) For every state s and instruction i, if evaluating the complete guard expression in s yields some false, then execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s): the outcome is the guard-false outcome carrying exactly the input state, so no machine-state component changes and no source operand is read. (b) For every state s, instruction i, and related state s', if AndB32Step s i s' and evalGuard s i.guard = some false, then s' = s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAndB32_guard_false_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
    execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)

theorem andB32Step_guard_false_frame
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (hstep : AndB32Step s i s')
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
    s' = s
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false (the complete guard expression evaluates false in s)
No source-resolution hypotheses are needed: the guard-false branch does not read source operands (this is part of the conclusion, not a precondition).
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (a) execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s); consequently the carried state equals the input state and the instruction has no state effect. (b) AndB32Step s i s' with evalGuard = some false forces s' = s.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-AND-SEM2-063 (guard-false state effect), source-resolved via SOURCE_FACT PTX-AND-SEM2-071 (section 9.7.13.2 clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.', CTX-08) and the derivation chain PTX-AND-SEM2-074 (CTX-07 'All PTX instructions may be predicated', CTX-02 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate', CTX-08 'If {!}p then instruction'); design dependency PTX-AND-SEM2-058 (two-case outcome, guardFalse carries the unchanged state). Source-non-reading in the guard-false branch is the mapping decision recorded by mapping-critic F-1.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: any state in which the referenced guard predicate is defined to false, or @!p with p true (the executable example @p with p = false keeps r1 at 5 demonstrates the behavior). The conclusion is not an element of the hypotheses; it pins the exact outcome constructor and the unchanged carried state, which is the semantic content of 'do nothing'.
strength_risks: The guard-false behavior must be presented as a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION from the explicit predication clause applied to and.b32 (PTX-AND-SEM2-063/074), never as an affirmative per-instruction SOURCE_FACT that the PTX and section itself states this.
The theorem is stated over the bounded model state pair; it does not by itself assert anything about components outside the model (deferred property PTX-AND-DEF-001).

Part (a)'s equality to ExecOutcome.guardFalse s (carrying exactly s) is a full state-preservation statement because guardFalse carries the whole MachineState and the only producer of guardFalse in execAndB32 is the unchanged input state.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Part (a): unfold execAndB32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some false branch, which returns some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s) directly; the source-evaluation branches are never reached, so no source-resolution case analysis is needed. Part (b): case on hstep; the executed constructor requires evalGuard = some true, which contradicts hguard (injectivity of some on Option Bool), so only the guardFalse constructor applies and s' = s.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-4 (guard-false frame); source-non-reading decision recorded at Gate C (mapping-critic F-1).

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the guard-behavior equivalence (semantics future topic PRF-5): on the approved well-formed lookup domain, an executed outcome occurs if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true. This covers the no-guard, @p, and @!p cases uniformly through evalGuard and pins the outcome classification of execAndB32. It complements PTX-AND-THM-006 (guard-false state preservation) by providing the reverse direction: an executed outcome implies the guard was true, so an instruction can never execute under a false complete guard. Because and.b32 has two source operands, the source-resolution hypothesis requires both a and b to resolve when the guard is true. The supporting guard-evaluation lemmas pin the per-constructor behavior of evalGuard (unguarded = true; @p = predicate value; @!p = negation) per PTX-AND-SEM2-029/035/043 and the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-AND-SEM2-030/072).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s and instruction i, if the complete guard expression resolves in s to some b and, when b is true, both sources resolve in s, then there exists an executed outcome from execAndB32 s i if and only if b is true. Equivalently: execution happens exactly when the complete guard expression is true; when b is false the outcome is the guard-false outcome (and, by PTX-AND-THM-006, the state is unchanged). Supporting lemmas: evalGuard s Guard.unguarded = some true; s.predRegs p = some true -> evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some true; s.predRegs p = some false -> evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some true; s.predRegs p = some false -> evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some false; s.predRegs p = some true -> evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some false.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem andB32_executes_iff_guard_true
    (s : MachineState) (i : AndB32Instruction) (b : Bool)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b)
    (hsources : b = true -> Exists fun (va : B32) => Exists fun (vb : B32) =>
        evalSourceA s i.a = some va /\ evalSourceB s i.b = some vb) :
    (Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
        execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true

-- supporting guard-evaluation lemmas (per-constructor evalGuard behavior)
theorem evalGuard_unguarded_true
    (s : MachineState) : evalGuard s Guard.unguarded = some true

theorem evalGuard_atPos_true
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some true) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some true

theorem evalGuard_atNeg_true_when_pred_false
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some false) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some true

theorem evalGuard_atPos_false
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some false) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some false

theorem evalGuard_atNeg_false_when_pred_true
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some true) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some false
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b (the complete guard expression resolves in s to b)
hsources : if b = true then both sources resolve in s: Exists va, Exists vb, evalSourceA s i.a = some va /\ evalSourceB s i.b = some vb
No additional guard or source preconditions.
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (Exists s', execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true; plus the per-constructor evalGuard lemmas.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED PTX-AND-SEM2-029 (guard representation and evaluation: unguarded true; @p value of p; @!p negation of value of p); DERIVED PTX-AND-SEM2-030 (execution condition iff complete guard expression true; grounded in CTX-08 'If {!}p then instruction' and CTX-02 'Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally'); DERIVED PTX-AND-SEM2-074 (derivation chain for and.b32 guard behavior); DERIVED PTX-AND-SEM2-033 (guard-true behavior); DERIVED PTX-AND-SEM2-035 (guard predicate read); DERIVED PTX-AND-SEM2-043 (PRE-5 guard well-typedness). Source evidence: CTX-02, CTX-07, CTX-08.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both directions are non-trivial. Forward: with b = true and hsources, the code reaches the executed branch. Reverse: with b = false, the code returns guardFalse, so no executed outcome exists. There exist states satisfying the hypotheses for both values of b (e.g., @p with p true and with p false; the @!p with p = false executable example shows r1 becoming 5 & 3 = 1), and the theorem's biconditional is false if the outcome classification were wrong, so it is not vacuous. The supporting evalGuard lemmas pin the per-constructor guard evaluation and distinguish @p from @!p (opposite execution conditions; PTX-AND-SEM2-029/035/043).
strength_risks: The theorem is a classification/guard-behavior statement, not a determinism claim; it must not be mistaken for PRF-1 (relational determinism, PTX-AND-THM-001) or for the functional single-valuedness of execAndB32.

The hypothesis shape must match the well-formed lookup domain exactly; adding source-resolution hypotheses unconditionally (even when b = false) would be an unapproved strengthening and would make the reverse direction trivial in a different way.
The supporting lemmas are simple definitional statements; they must not be presented as deep semantic theorems, only as the per-constructor guard evaluation facts behind PRF-5.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAndB32. Forward direction: assume b = true, use hsources to obtain va and vb; evalGuard gives some true, evalSourceA for i.a gives some va and evalSourceB for i.b gives some vb, so the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed _). Reverse direction: assume Exists s', execAndB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s'); the evalGuard match in execAndB32 must have taken the some true branch (the some false branch returns guardFalse and the none branch returns none), hence b = true (use hguard and injectivity of some). The supporting lemmas unfold evalGuard and evaluate the match on the constructor.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-5 (guard behavior: executes iff complete guard expression true, covering no-guard, @p, @!p uniformly).
